## TL;DR

Human-assigned tasks now get a shared `humanTaskGuideWarning()` that warns when `## Step-by-step guide` is missing, only scaffold placeholder text remains, or the heading appears only inside fenced code. Warnings flow through CLI create/update, HTTP task APIs, and a drawer banner (`data-test-id="human-guide-warning"`). PM and engineer default prompts plus the PM split-human-step canned message require a filled guide. Review feedback was addressed with fence-aware section detection, corrected handoff shot fixture (`drawer:humanGuideWarning`), and import/test cleanup.

## Work and rationale

The motivating gap was human-held tasks filed as two-line acceptance criteria with no actionable steps. Enforcement is intentionally soft (warning, not a hard error) so existing human tasks keep working while new and updated tasks get immediate feedback. Centralizing logic in `src/core/task-underspecified.ts` keeps CLI, server, and Vue drawer aligned and matches how `needs-human-step` and underspecified checks already live in that module.

The scaffold from `HUMAN_TASK_SCAFFOLD` and the human-step split template both ship italic placeholder lines. Treating “heading present” as sufficient would defeat the feature, so `humanTaskGuideSectionFilled()` requires at least one numbered step line (`^\d+\. `) after stripping known placeholder strings. That yields two distinct messages: missing heading versus unfilled scaffold.

Agent guidance was updated in `config.ts` defaults for PM and engineer roles, in `splitHumanStepRequirementsPrompt()` / `PM_SPLIT_HUMAN_STEP_MESSAGE`, and in `human-step-tags.ts` for split bodies. Docs: one line in `AGENTS.md`, `docs/agent-workflow-rules.md`, and `user-docs/cli.md` including `--section "Step-by-step guide"` editing.

## Approaches tried

Early implementation used `extractSection()` only, which satisfied the literal acceptance criterion but let empty scaffolds through; review round 3 called that out. The filled-section heuristic and separate unfilled warning closed the gap without blocking `repoos new --human` (authors still get the scaffold, then see “still empty” until they add steps).

For false positives from markdown samples quoting the heading, fence-aware `extractHumanTaskGuideSection()` mirrors the pattern used in task summary validation: skip ```/~~~ blocks when locating the real section.

The UI shot initially used `card:humanStep`, which seeds a different fixture and timed out waiting for the banner. The declared shot now uses `drawer:humanGuideWarning` with route `/work?task=9999&tab=changes` and `waitFor` on `[data-test-id="human-guide-warning"]`.

## Challenges and blockers

A merge from `main` conflicted on sibling `work/*.md` files; resolving with main’s copies was attempted but the merge was aborted to avoid landing unrelated bookkeeping on the branch without a concluded merge commit. `src/ui-app/tests/pm-canned-messages.test.ts` has no diff against `main` on this branch, so the review’s conflict note does not apply to current tree state.

`repoos check --changed main` is long-running; one run failed on `check-fmt` (fixed with `bun run fmt`) and another on `rendered-contrast`, which may be environmental/flaky and was re-run in isolation.

## Key learnings

Human-task contracts differ from agent tasks: warnings and scaffolds fit better than extending `underspecified` or hard validation. Any UI surface for the warning needs a dedicated shot fixture so preview capture does not depend on production board data. Built-in prompts must be updated everywhere canned server messages are assembled, not only in `config.ts`, or PM split flows will still omit guide instructions.
